title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: arXiv:2610.35962v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalC

translated_title: h1：自动定理证明领域“苦涩教训”的初尝
translated_abstract: 尽管非形式数学的进步在很大程度上来自于扩展前沿语言模型的思维链和智能体推理能力，但形式定理证明却日益依赖于围绕这些模型构建的人类设计工作流，例如规划、分解以及协调专门的证明器。这引出了一个“苦涩教训”式的问题：一个简单且能扩展测试时计算量的智能体循环，能否与这些复杂工作流相匹敌？这个问题的答案至关重要，因为形式化验证必须同步扩展，才能跟上前沿模型产出研究级数学内容的速度；然而新的工作流很少能回答这一问题，因为其收益往往与更强的模型或更多的计算量混杂在一起，难以区分。我们通过 h1 来研究这一问题：h1 是一个简单的框架，它为模型提供一个与 Lean 4 交互的高效接口，并通过验证器反馈和自我反思让模型持续工作，而不强加任何分解或搜索结构。h1 在 PutnamBench、FATE-X 和 FormalC 上达到了最先进的结果。
tldr: 论文提出 h1——一个仅依赖 Lean 4 接口、验证器反馈与自我反思的简单智能体框架，无需人工设计的规划或分解结构，仅靠扩展测试时计算便在 PutnamBench 等基准上达到最先进水平，印证了自动定理证明中的“苦涩教训”。
en_tdlr: h1, a simple agentic harness that scales test-time compute through a Lean 4 interface, verifier feedback, and self-reflection—without imposing human-designed decomposition or search—achieves state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalC, echoing the Bitter Lesson in automated theorem proving.
